audits.title: 522 Audit of Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Bleed Management in a District General Hospital
audits.standard: BSG guidelines on acute lower GI bleeding (Oakland score, investigation and management)
audits.setting: District general hospital (Musgrove Park Hospital, Taunton affiliation)

cycle1.result: 10 (13.2%) Oakland ≤8, 19 ≤9, 57 (75%) ≥10; of 66 'major' bleeds 41 (62.1%) had no colonoscopy.

audits.other_findings: Of 19 same-day discharges, 3 (15.8%) scored ≤8; of 23 overnight admissions 5 (21.7%) scored ≤8.
audits.citation: Mallick S, Salem R, Payne A. 522 Audit of Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Bleed Management in a District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.444.

audits.title: SP4.2.1 Emergency management of lower GI bleeds: a full-cycle audit of practice at a district general hospital
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology 2019 lower GI bleeding guidelines (admission advised for Oakland score >8)
audits.setting: District general hospital, surgical wards and surgical assessment unit (West Hertfordshire / Barking, Havering and Redbridge)

cycle1.result: 37/47 (78.7%) had major LGIB, of whom 6 (16%) were discharged the same day; inpatient endoscopy 14.9%; 0% of unstable patients had CT angiogram on admission.

audits.intervention: Departmental teaching session and posters of BSG guidelines on surgical wards and surgical assessment unit

cycle2.result: 29/30 (96.7%) had major LGIB and none were discharged the same day; inpatient endoscopy 66.7%; 50% of unstable patients had CT angiogram on admission.

audits.other_findings: Of 10/47 minor LGIB in cycle 1, 6 (60%) were discharged the same day; impact on clinical outcomes not yet assessed.
audits.citation: Khanderia E, Patel R, Chandegra R, Gass H, Doshi A, Morsy H, et al.. SP4.2.1 Emergency management of lower GI bleeds: a full-cycle audit of practice at a district general hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac247.045.

audits.title: TU8.5 Management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB) remains largely conservative and the impact of BSG recommendations largely unseen: results of a 4 year audit
audits.standard: BSG guidelines for acute lower GI bleeding and the 2015 UK nationwide LGIB audit
audits.setting: Emergency General Surgical Unit, Wirral University Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: Oakland score used as a discharge criterion in 7.1%.

audits.intervention: Publication of BSG guidelines (no local intervention described).
audits.other_findings: 98 patients across both periods; readmission 19%, median stay 2.7 days, CT 41.8% and colonoscopy/flexible sigmoidoscopy 65.3%; no angioembolisation.
audits.citation: Ahmed S, Patten A, Guy R. TU8.5 Management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB) remains largely conservative and the impact of BSG recommendations largely unseen: results of a 4 year audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.078.

audits.title: TH3.2 Audit of acute lower GI bleed admissions - outcomes and management
audits.standard: BSG 2019 UK national guideline on lower GI bleeding
audits.setting: Emergency department and surgical assessment unit, NHS Dumfries & Galloway

cycle1.result: 3 had Oakland score ≤8 (1 hospitalised); 21 had OS >8, 7 of whom were discharged; of 14 (51.8%) on anticoagulants/antiplatelets, 10 had drugs suspended appropriately and 2 did not.

audits.intervention: Checklist based on the guidelines developed.
audits.other_findings: Eight referred for outpatient endoscopy; duration to colonoscopy needs improvement.
audits.citation: Sami S, Hemadasa N, Loh C, DeCruz A, Mirza M. TH3.2 Audit of acute lower GI bleed admissions - outcomes and management. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.208.

audits.title: 1293 Audit of Initial Management of Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding as per the British Society of Gastroenterology Guidelines
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines on lower GI bleeding (Oakland score, shock index)
audits.setting: Emergency Department, George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Of 45 major bleeds, 4 unstable (1 CT angiogram); 32 admitted (71.1%), 13 discharged (28.9%), 5 without endoscopy; 3 (23.1%) readmitted within 28 days.

audits.intervention: Efforts to integrate the BSG guidelines (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Of 27 major bleeds, 2 unstable (1 CT angiogram); 15 admitted (55.6%), 12 discharged (44.4%), all with endoscopy; 1 (8.3%) readmitted within 28 days.

audits.other_findings: Minimal improvement in Oakland score compliance; all minor bleeds (Oakland 8 or less) discharged without readmission.
audits.citation: Gibbs A, Rutherfurd A, Sivakumar N, Zehra S, Zohdy M, Marimuthu K. 1293 Audit of Initial Management of Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding as per the British Society of Gastroenterology Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.313.

audits.title: 1048 Evaluating Inpatient Management of Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding - A Retrospective Single Centre Audit
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology LGIB guidelines
audits.setting: District general hospital, Mid Yorkshire NHS Teaching Trust, Wakefield

cycle1.result: 11 (25%) had no imaging, treatment or procedure; 6 (14%) unnecessary admissions per BSG criteria; 7 (16%) transfused, 3 (7%) not meeting BSG criteria; 2 (5%) CT angiogram with Shock Index <1; 4 (9%) with Shock Index >1 had no CT angiogram.

audits.other_findings: 3 (7%) had inpatient flexible sigmoidoscopy despite haemodynamic stability; virtual wards suggested to prevent unnecessary admissions.
audits.citation: Sharif F, Oldfield T, Alomari L, Baik S, Aftab N. 1048 Evaluating Inpatient Management of Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding - A Retrospective Single Centre Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.302.

audits.title: 790 Management of Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding in a District General Hospital- Clinical Audit
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines on lower GI bleeding
audits.setting: Medway NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital, Gillingham
audits.intervention: Educational posters and email summarising BSG guidelines and audit recommendations.

cycle2.result: DRE compliance 91%; TXA use 38%; CT-A 19%; Oakland score documentation unchanged.

audits.other_findings: Oakland score documentation did not improve.

audits.title: TPTh 3.09 Audit of Diagnosis and Management of Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Tract Bleeding (LGIB) in a Rural General Hospital, can we reduce hospital admissions?
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology 2019 LGIB guidelines (Oakland score for safe discharge)
audits.setting: Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth, rural general hospital

cycle1.result: 13 minor and 60 major by Oakland score; 4 discharged same day; median stay 3 days; 72% managed conservatively; 18 transfused, 3 had surgery.

audits.other_findings: Commonest causes were diverticular disease (45%) and haemorrhoids (17%). Oakland score judged insufficiently accurate for safe discharge.
audits.citation: Mohamed S, Chan O, Akhtar H, El-sayed S, Kirkland E, Sebastiani S. TPTh 3.09 Audit of Diagnosis and Management of Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Tract Bleeding (LGIB) in a Rural General Hospital, can we reduce hospital admissions?. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.447.
